label: q as first token, or <DEL> step (sequence-dependent)
explanation: Two unrelated components. (1) Input q at step 0: fires on every such step (precision 1.0), at moderate magnitude (~0.17 of max), about 23% of activation mass. Later q inputs in the original phase fire less reliably, and so do y and a. (2) The <DEL> delimiter step: about 50% of activation mass and all of the strongest activations (up to 1.0 of max). It fires on only about 5% of delimiter steps, though, and which ones depends on the sequence contents in a diffuse way: it is enriched when the first original token (the one about to be output) is 2/i/k/h/o/m/u/w, when z or n appeared earlier, and in longer sequences (L 8-9). This conjunction reaches only about 0.3 precision. Weak, scattered activations also occur in the copy phase (about 17% of mass), mostly at recall_idx 1-4. Rare on most other letters and digits in the original phase. Dev F1 0.47.
